extracted.intended_audience: NIA K99/R00 review committee (grant reviewers) and grant mentors/collaborators
extracted.subtask_description: Portions of an NIH K99/R00 grant application (research strategy, training in RCR, benchmarks, mentorship and letters of support) describing expectations, benchmarks, training, and mentoring commitments for a postdoctoral-to-independent investigator career-development award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarks for Success
rubrics_metrics.description: A. We will obtain 4 publications in peer-reviewed journals [directly related to this study]: 1) study of FCG and clinician perspectives on challenges, strategies, and gaps in home hospice care for PwD (K99), 2) developing training and tool (K99), 3) pilot testing and revising training and tool (R00), and 4) preliminary efficacy of training and tool (R00). [I (Dr. Luth) will publish an additional 2-3 papers a year on topic using data generated from this project and from other sources.] B. We will present study results annually at national conferences and through invitations to speak locally to relevant stakeholder groups and institutions. C. We will have sufficient data and information for a competitive R01 application for a fully powered RCT to test training and tool in other hospice settings (rural) and/or with larger or different populations (e.g. more hospices, Latinx FCG). D. I (Dr. Luth) will launch as independent investigator with necessary expertise and skills to become a leading expert in improving hospice care for PwD and FCG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies concrete, time-linked products and career outcomes expected from the K99/R00: a set number of study-related publications, annual dissemination activities, data sufficient for an R01, and career launch to independence. Also notes additional yearly publications beyond the 4 study-focused papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 5 outlines the timeline for research activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeline/benchmarks should be provided in a table (Table 5) aligning activities to K99 and R00 phases; page references the table as the formal schedule of activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor of Prior Research and Current Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigorous research exists on supporting FCG and community-dwelling PwD at early and middle stages of dementia and the EOL for PwD in nursing homes. However, very few projects focus on PwD in home hospice care, and none focus on the needs of African American PwD and FCG. This project addresses the lack of research on PwD in home hospice... We will use an RCT, a methodologically rigorous approach, to determining the preliminary efficacy of the intervention we propose to develop and pilot test. We will register this pilot test on ClinicalTrials.gov so that other researchers may reproduce and extend our findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes methodological rigor (RCT design) appropriate to pilot efficacy testing, situates project in literature gaps, and requires prospective registration to promote reproducibility and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex as a Biological Variable and Authentication of Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants will not be excluded based on sex or gender. Over 60% of FCG and 72% of hospice clinicians are female, so we expect the majority of our FCG and clinician participants to be female. We will monitor recruitment based on sex/gender. In the event that a patient sex/gender is under-represented (<30%), we will modify recruitment strategies to target the under-represented group. This study does not use biological or chemical resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires active monitoring of sex/gender representation with a concrete under-representation threshold (<30%) that triggers changes to recruitment strategies; also documents authentication (no biological/chemical resources used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) Training Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: As a graduate student and post-doctoral fellow, Dr. Luth completed several courses in research ethics and responsible conduct of research. Most recently (December 2017), she completed the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) course offered by the WCM Clinical and Translational Science Center (CTSC). Dr. Luth has also completed the online Collaborative Institutional Training Initiative (CITI) course in The Protection of Human Research Subjects; she will complete the CITI refresher course every four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies formal coursework completion and periodic refreshers (CITI every four years); documents plan to reenroll in institutional RCR course (e.g., Fall 2021) and ongoing one-on-one mentor discussions to uphold ethical research practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR Course Content and Format
rubrics_metrics.description: The course includes 9 online modules with exams (3 hours total) and 5 in-person discussion groups (11 hours total). Specific topics include: (1) research misconduct, including whistleblowing and dispute resolution; (2) data acquisition, management, sharing, and ownership; (3) animal welfare; (4) use of human subjects; (5) conflicts of interest; (6) authorship and responsible publication practices; (7) peer review; (8) collaboration and mentoring; (9) the role of the scientist in social responsibility and export control; and (10) rigor and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the expected curricular content and approximate contact hours for institutional RCR training; highlights explicit topics reviewers expect applicants to have covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty Involvement in RCR Training and Oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: In developing the proposed research, Dr. Luth and her mentorship team have discussed the importance of responsible conduct of research with vulnerable older adult populations. These discussions have centered around informed consent procedures, recruitment of study participants from hospice, and ensuring family caregiver autonomy when the tool is being used. Over the course of the grant period, Dr. Prigerson will oversee Dr. Luth’s RCR training and ensure that she completes the coursework outlined above. Dr. Prigerson will also provide ongoing education around research ethnics, especially as they pertain to conducting research in health care contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor(s) must actively oversee RCR training, provide ongoing ethics education tailored to vulnerable populations and clinical settings, and advise on informed consent and recruitment practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and Transparency (ClinicalTrials.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will register this pilot test on ClinicalTrials.gov so that other researchers may reproduce and extend our findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot studies intended to test interventions should be prospectively registered to ensure transparency and reproducibility; registration is treated as part of methodological rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Diverse Populations and Cultural Sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Very few projects focus on PwD in home hospice care, and none focus on the needs of African American PwD and FCG... She has considered how racial disparities may arise at all stages of the project and has taken steps to minimize them in her study design... taking steps to ensure that the training and tool are culturally inclusive and sensitive to the differing needs of individuals from diverse backgrounds... incorporate implicit bias awareness and overlay cultural sensitivity and inclusivity throughout the clinician training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations include explicit attention to racial/ethnic disparities in study design, culturally inclusive intervention development, and training that addresses implicit bias; recruitment and formative work should reflect targeted inclusion of underrepresented groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship Plan: Roles, Activities, and Meeting Frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: We have established a productive relationship in the last 2 years and will continue to meet weekly for the duration of her K99 award. These meetings will allow me to support her progress toward her career development and research goals and to complete the annual progress reports for the K99 award... I will meet with Dr. Luth monthly to review progress on her project and towards her career and development goals. I will help her strategize about her training and research and how to disseminate her findings... I will meet with her at least quarterly to discuss her progress towards her career development goals and advise her on study design and will be available more frequently as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentorship commitments should specify frequency (weekly, monthly, quarterly), concrete mentor duties (oversight of progress, career development, assistance with grant writing and dissemination, completing progress reports), and availability; a team-based mentoring structure with delegated responsibilities is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor Qualifications and Institutional Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: My track record as a continuously-funded, R01-level NIH-funded investigator for over 20 years, starting with my own K award, will allow me to advise and support Libby... I have received multiple mentoring awards, including Harvard Medical School’s Clifford Barger Excellence in Mentoring Award... The Cornell Center for Research on End-of-Life Care I direct, creates a resource-rich environment to provide additional support for Libby’s research efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers expect mentors with a strong funding and mentoring track record, relevant scientific expertise, and institutional resources/centers that provide a supportive training environment; documenting mentor accomplishments strengthens the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot Testing Participant/Clinician Selection Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: We will include clinicians who have both African American and white patients on their caseloads in pilot testing and help clinicians identify which patients on caseloads to use when testing the tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot testing procedures should ensure clinicians have experience with diverse patient groups and should include explicit strategies to identify appropriate patient-caregiver dyads for testing the intervention/tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and Stakeholder Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: We will present study results annually at national conferences and through invitations to speak locally to relevant stakeholder groups and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should include regular dissemination (annual national conference presentations and local invited talks) and engagement with stakeholder organizations to promote uptake and awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility, Practicality, and Scalability of Intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Her study also reflects her commitment to developing practical, clinically useful, and scalable interventions that are intended to account for and complement existing care delivery practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interventions should be designed to be pragmatic and feasible within real-world hospice care settings, compatible with existing workflows, and scalable to other settings/populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation for Future Funding / Transition to Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: We will have sufficient data and information for a competitive R01 application for a fully powered RCT to test training and tool in other hospice settings (rural) and/or with larger or different populations... I (Dr. Luth) will launch as independent investigator with necessary expertise and skills to become a leading expert...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The K99/R00 plan should generate pilot data and career development such that the applicant can submit a competitive R01 and successfully transition to independent investigator status; mentorship should explicitly support R00/R01 preparation and job search activities.
